title: Oracle C2M DevOps Release Management & CI/CD Automation
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Oracle Utilities C2M + WebLogic 14c administration; middleware/database/integration work, production-impact care).

Oracle Utilities C2M/CC&B/MDM + WebLogic 14c authored from Oracle's official product + OUAF docs; version-specific details (C2M 25.4/min v2.9, WebLogic 14c) cited or flagged 'verify for your version'; My-Oracle-Support-gated patches/notes are pointed to, not reproduced. Automation is WLST (Jython)/shell/SQL, not PowerShell.
hook: Automate C2M releases — repeatable, governed, hands-off
problem: Manual C2M releases are slow and error-prone. This solution establishes DevOps release management and CI/CD for Oracle C2M: a pipeline for building, promoting, and deploying OUAF config and code across environments, with automation for the routine admin tasks — so releases are repeatable, governed, and fast, pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the C2M DevOps model: source control for OUAF config/code, a build/promote/deploy pipeline, and automation of routine admin.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (CI/CD tooling, source control, environment access, migration/CMA tooling).

Implementation Guide — exact steps to define the pipeline (build → migrate config → deploy → validate), wire automation for routine tasks (restarts, checks, promotions), add gates/rollback, and validate, pilot-first.

5 automation scripts (WLST/Jython, shell & SQL) — environment/config discovery, per-node validation, a health/coverage report, safe remediation (dry-run by default), and a scope/target helper — authentic to C2M & WebLogic administration.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (pipeline runs, deploys succeed, rollback works) plus Best Practices for governed, automated releases.
short: Establish DevOps release management and CI/CD for C2M — a build/promote/deploy pipeline plus routine-task automation — so releases are repeatable, governed, and fast, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
